paragraphs: 6 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Sunday for 6 clubs across 4 levels, with Brooks Lee producing the night's most notable performance.

Brooks Lee's home run — his 20th of the season came in the fifth inning on a 3-2 92 mph cutter from Walker Buehler. The swing moved the score from 0-1 to 1-1. Statcast measured the ball at 101.7 mph off the bat, a 28-degree launch angle, 401 feet.
Brooks Lee went 1-for-3, 1 home run, 1 RBI, 1 run scored.
He batted sixth and started at third base.
Minnesota Twins fell to San Diego Padres, 1-8.

Alejandro Garza went 1-for-5, 2 RBI for Hill City Howlers at Single-A. Alejandro Garza tied the game in the eighth with a two-run single to right field on the first pitch from Riley Stanford, changing the score from 3-5 to 5-5. He batted first and started at second base. Hill City Howlers fell to Charleston RiverDogs, 6-7.

Zach Daudet went 0-for-3, 1 walk for Asheville Tourists at High-A. Zach Daudet produced a flyout in the sixth to left field on a 1-0 pitch from Elwis Mijares. He batted sixth and started at shortstop. Asheville Tourists fell to Brooklyn Cyclones, 1-12.
Ryan Tayman went 0-for-5 for St. Lucie Mets at Single-A. He batted fourth and started at designated hitter. St. Lucie Mets fell to Lakeland Flying Tigers, 2-12.

Bryce Warrecker came on in relief for Hudson Valley Renegades in the bottom of the seventh with nobody out. He worked 2.0 innings, allowing 2 hits and 1 earned run, with 2 walks. Hudson Valley Renegades beat Jersey Shore BlueClaws, 5-4.

Steven Brooks came on in relief for Portland Sea Dogs in the top of the fifth with nobody out. He worked 0 2/3 innings, allowing 0 hits and 2 earned runs, with 5 walks and 1 strikeout. One of his strikeouts came in the fifth on a 1-2 pitch, when he put away Bryson Ware. Portland Sea Dogs fell to Reading Fightin Phils, 3-10.
title: Brooks Lee delivers in a key spot
